summary: Human-factors research supports the risk of losing situation awareness at high automation levels and the value of adaptive control. It is adjacent evidence: no controlled study yet establishes the correct abstraction-switch threshold for coding-agent operations.

items.text: Endsley and Kiris (1995) experimentally studied out-of-the-loop performance with automation and found degraded situation awareness and recovery performance after automation failure, motivating retained drill-down and practice.

Gutman et al. (2021) evaluated levels of automation and workload with 80 participants, providing adjacent evidence that the best control level depends on workload and task context rather than a universal maximum.
Research on adaptive automation (2003) examines dynamic changes in allocation between humans and automation, supporting explicit transition criteria while remaining outside software-agent delivery.
